dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?
Hi, good afternoon Denise. My name is Deirdre Brennan. I am calling for my mother, she has an old appliance she wants to get rid of. A washing machine. How do we get it hauled away?
Okay, a washer. Is it going out to the curb for pickup, or are you hoping to bring it somewhere yourselves?
Um, curb is better. My mother cannot lift, and I do not have a truck. So curb, yes. If the city can take it.
Generally, large items like appliances aren't picked up with your regular trash. They need to be scheduled as a bulk pickup, so I'd set that up with you. Do you want me to do that now?
Yes, please. But first, is there a fee? Do we pay for this? I have the paper from the city here in front of me, the trash calendar, but I do not see the word for appliance.

There can be a charge for some appliances, especially ones with refrigerant like a fridge or an AC unit. A washer is usually simpler. I don't have the exact amount in front of me, so I'll have the bulk pickup desk confirm it when they schedule you. Do you have a minute while I check how they do the scheduling?
Yes, yes, I have time. I am on my lunch break. I work at a marina office, so I have the desk and all the paper here. It is quiet today because of the storm.
Oh, that's right, it's coming in today. Are you getting wind over there already?
A little. The boats are all tied up twice, my boss said. So, okay. The washer. It is not a very big one, it is the old kind, top loading.

That's fine. Top loader is good. [pause] Okay, so here's what I've got. Bulk items have to be called in ahead of time, and with the storm this weekend, collection could be pushed a day or so. Nothing goes out to the curb until you have a date, because we don't want it blowing around.
Yes, that makes sense. So no curb today. Not today.
Right, not today. I'd say wait until after the storm clears. I'll put in the request and they'll give you the date and the fee, if there is one, when they call back. What's the best number?
The number is four-zero-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-one. That is four-zero-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-one.
Got it, four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-one. And I'll need the pickup address, the one where the washer is.
Oh, um, I think I do not give the address on this call. Can the person who calls back take it? I am at work and my mother is the one on the account.

Hmm, we really do need the address to schedule it. Let me put your name and number down with a note that it's a top-loading washer, and the desk will get the address from you when they call. Is that okay?
Yes, that is okay. Thank you. So they call me, and they tell me the fee and the date. And I give the address then.
Exactly. Usually within a business day or two, though a storm might slow it. If you don't hear by early next week, call us back.
Early next week. Okay. Should I take the door off the washer or anything? I read about that somewhere, for the refrigerators.
That's for fridges, mostly. For a washer, just empty it out, make sure the hoses are disconnected, and keep the lid taped down if you can. The crew will tell you if there's anything else.
Hoses disconnected, lid taped. Okay, good. My mother will be happy, she has been looking at this machine in the garage for a long time.
I'm sure. Well, we'll get it out of there. Anything else I can help with today?
No, that is all. You were very helpful, Denise. Thank you so much. Stay safe in the storm.
You too, hon. Tell your boss to keep those boats tied down. Bye now.
I will. Bye bye.
